## The Future
The path forward is clear--we must end this genocide, release all hostages, end the occupation, rebuild Gaza, ensure a viable two state solution, and hold accountable those who committed war crimes.
But the question is whether American leadership has the moral and ethical courage to walk that path? A path that _should_ start with President Biden. Instead, we see an expanding conflict that threatens to engulf the entire region. Asked if he supports Israel striking Iran's oil refineries, Biden responded, "[We're discussing that](https://substack.com/redirect/47b55c25-0a9f-4e36-84e5-f77e29f10094?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." This answer is perplexing and confounding. Biden himself [admits he believes Netanyahu is perpetuating war to help Trump win](https://substack.com/redirect/754b6526-5642-4898-8a67-140f35ee8d9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), yet Biden continues to arm Netanyahu to perpetuate war. Politically, I believe Harris can beat Trump--but I do not know if she can beat Trump _and_ Biden if Biden continues to betray the will of the American people. We know [the following critical facts](https://substack.com/redirect/12980122-2d54-4e69-8608-70e4c15ac87b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about how united Americans are to end the siege on Gaza by withholding arms from Netanyahu:
* 61% of Americans oppose weapons to Israel's assault in Gaza
* 77% of Democrats reject US weapons to Israel
* 63% of moderates reject US weapons to Israel

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bd602c92-9126-4a18-9da0-39cf2b2b5384?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And we also know that the American people want Harris to break from Biden. As CNN reports regarding [a national study on this very question](https://substack.com/redirect/0ca1ef7e-8ea2-411a-aaf4-b8961cc62e4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> In mid-September, the Democratic research and polling initiative [Blueprint conducted a national poll testing a long series of potential statements](https://substack.com/redirect/9c3d0e82-dcc7-4aea-83db-8bfc5f821999?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Harris could make about herself and Biden. Those that performed best, the polling found, "were those that displayed a clear break between her and Biden," while those that performed worst were "those that portrayed a future Harris administration as building on the accomplishments of the Biden era."
And finally, we know this is not a position unique to Americans. This is an area of agreement between Americans, Israelis, hostage families, and Palestinians. It's also global consensus with our main allies. Canada and the United Kingdom are already restricting arms to Netanyahu. France is now calling to end all arms to Netanyahu. And Ireland refuses to remove its peacekeepers from Lebanon even as Netanyahu bombs Lebanon. Yet--President Biden continues to defy the American people and the Leahy Laws to keep arming Netanyahu. If [Ronald Reagan could force Israel to stop bombing civilians with a single phone call](https://substack.com/redirect/6e74099e-3195-4af1-b743-a4d4ee500418?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), why is Joe Biden afraid to stop arming Israel to commit war crimes?
## Where do we go from here
Last week I attended a fundraiser for Gaza with MedGlobal. And in the powerful display of witness testimonies from Gaza, we were reminded the names of Hind Rajab, the 6-year-old Palestinian girl that Israeli forces shot to death with more than 300 bullets. We were reminded of the two aid workers, Yousef Zeino and Ahmed al Madhoun, who the Red Crescent deployed to save Hind with the permission of the Israeli military--who then killed Yousef and Ahmed anyway. We were reminded of Refaat Alareer, a Palestinian writer, poet, professor, and activist from the Gaza Strip that the Israeli military murdered with a targeted drone strike. And we were reminded above all else, that these are not statistics, these are human beings. And it is indefensible for the US government to continue to fund a genocide, especially while knowing full well that Israel's current leader has no intention of establishing peace.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be1d41b6-2539-48a7-8b6e-72e30af70b27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Israeli military shot Hind Rajab (6) more than 300 times as she was trapped under a car, murdering her.
Justice dictates we boldly and courageously walk the path of peace for the sake of humanity. It is imperative that we as Americans, and indeed as all people globally committed to justice and humanity, exert all our efforts to secure that permanent and lasting ceasefire and release of all hostages, meaningful resources to rebuild Gaza and Palestine into a sovereign state, and meaningful accountability for those who committed these war crimes. If you have influence over politicians, speak to them. If you have resources to donate to relief agencies, donate. And if all you have is your voice to speak up for justice, then let your voice be heard.
Indeed, if you've ever looked at historical atrocities and asked yourself, "_What would I have done if I were alive then_?" the answer is, it's whatever you're doing right now to stop the genocide in Gaza.
I close with the poem of Refaat Alareer. May our better angels enable us to bring back love.

### "IF I MUST DIE" _BY REFAAT ALAREER_
If I must die,
you must live
to tell my story
to sell my things
to buy a piece of cloth
and some strings,
(make it white with a long tail)
so that a child, somewhere in Gaza
while looking heaven in the eye
awaiting his dad who left in a blaze--
and bid no one farewell
not even to his flesh
not even to himself--
sees the kite, my kite you made, flying up above
and thinks for a moment an angel is there
bringing back love
If I must die
let it bring hope
let it be a tale

And it is indefensible for the US government to continue to fund a genocide, especially while knowing full well that Israel's current leader has no intention of establishing peace. | | ---|---|--- The Israeli military shot Hind Rajab (6) more than 300 times as she was trapped under a car, murdering her. Justice dictates we boldly and courageously walk the path of peace for the sake of humanity. It is imperative that we as Americans, and indeed as all people globally committed to justice and humanity, exert all our efforts to secure that permanent and lasting ceasefire and release of all hostages, meaningful resources to rebuild Gaza and Palestine into a sovereign state, and meaningful accountability for those who committed these war crimes. If you have influence over politicians, speak to them. If you have resources to donate to relief agencies, donate. And if all you have is your voice to speak up for justice, then let your voice be heard. Indeed, if you've ever looked at historical atrocities and asked yourself, "What would I have done if I were alive then?" the answer is, it's whatever you're doing right now to stop the genocide in Gaza. I close with the poem of Refaat Alareer. May our better angels enable us to bring back love. "IF I MUST DIE" BY REFAAT ALAREER If I must die, you must live to tell my story to sell my things to buy a piece of cloth and some strings, (make it white with a long tail) so that a child, somewhere in Gaza while looking heaven in the eye awaiting his dad who left in a blaze-- and bid no one farewell not even to his flesh not even to himself-- sees the kite, my kite you made, flying up above and thinks for a moment an angel is there bringing back love If I must die let it bring hope let it be a tale | | ---|---|--- In a march for Palestine, activists honor Refaat and carry his poem and his kite. name: CADEM Organizing
subject: October 2024 Organizing Newsletter
body:
| | | | |
---
| The California Democratic Party’s Organizing Department is excited to highlight the stories of our team members who are passionate about making a difference throughout our state. From leading our organizing efforts to connecting with local community leaders, our organizing team is working in every corner of California to ensure we continue to elect Democrats up and down the ballot.
---
| Your county elections office will begin mailing ballots by October 7, 2024. The California Democratic Party has compiled a list of Voter Resources. Please click on the buttons below.
---
[CADEM Voter Resources](https://cadem.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=937cb8fef613f2c2cf80bf894&id=8f55f37977&e=ceda8b4f9a)
[CADEM Voter Education Social Kit](https://cadem.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=937cb8fef613f2c2cf80bf894&id=55044163f6&e=ceda8b4f9a)
| **Elizabeth Gonzales-Cortes****Intern**
---
| My name is Elizabeth Gonzales-Cortes and I am a student at UC Irvine. Originally from Madera, I became a Democrat because of my strong commitment to addressing health-related issues. This passion drives me to advocate for policies and initiatives that promote public health, illness prevention, and access to health care. I am dedicated to educating young voters on how to make informed decisions and ensure their voices are heard in this election.
---
|
---
| **Bahar Babagoli****Intern**
---
| As a senior at Chapman University studying Psychology and Political Science, my Iranian-American heritage has deeply influenced my commitment to advocacy, particularly in healthcare access and human rights. Inspired by movements like Women, Life, Freedom in Iran, I've joined the Public Affairs Alliance of Iranian Americans to challenge oppressive regimes. Additionally, I'm an active participant in the California Democratic Party, working to boost voter turnout and support for Democratic candidates, including Vice President Kamala Harris and Governor Tim Walz. My efforts extend to promoting environmentalism and educating young voters on political issues.
---
|
---
| **Pamela Perez****Intern**
---
| I’m a San Diego native and a student at Chapman University. As a first-time organizer, my involvement with the Student Government Association has deepened my skills in campaigning and outreach. I identify as a Democrat, advocating for a democratic nation that values choice and compromise. I’m passionate about reforming immigration and tackling income inequality. Currently, as a youth voter engagement intern for CADEM, I lead voter registration drives for young and underrepresented communities, emphasizing the importance of elections through canvassing, phone banking, and social media outreach.
---
|
---
| **Samantha Toledo****Intern**
---
| I’m from Fresno, California, and currently a student at Fresno City College. My commitment to California Democrats stems from my upbringing as the child of immigrant parents, which exposed me to the impact of political decisions on working families. This motivates my advocacy for an inclusive society that champions immigrant rights, affordable education, and equal opportunity.
As an organizer, I work to uplift women's rights, especially reproductive freedom, and advocate for equity in education, economic justice, and immigration reform. To strengthen the Democratic presence in California, I engage voters through door-to-door canvassing and organize voter registration events in low-turnout communities. My goal is to expand access to voting and empower voters to support Democratic candidates, helping us secure vital battleground seats.
---
| The California Democratic Party is mobilizing to engage our battleground districts! Through longterm organizing efforts, we are working tirelessly to elect people-powered leaders who truly represent the will of the people. From city council races to state assembly, senate seats, and congressional offices, our dedicated volunteers are out every day connecting with voters and emphasizing the importance of this election season. Everyday, we host phone banks, text banks, and voter outreach events to support Democrats across Northern California, the Central Valley, Antelope Valley, Santa Clarita, San Fernando Valley, Riverside County, Orange County, and beyond.
---
|
---
| **Organizing for Jessica Morse for CA-03, Porsche Middleton for AD-7, ****Neva Parker for AD-5, and Hla Elkhatib Folsom City Council**
---
|
---
| **Organizing for Adam Gray for CA-3, Esmeralda Soria for AD-27, ****& Jessica Self for AD-22**
---
|
---
| **Organizing for George Whitesides for CA-27, Kipp Mueller for SD-23, Pilar Schiavo for AD-40, Ricardo Ortega for AD-34, Juan Carrillo for AD-39**
---
|
---
| **Organizing for Will Rollins for CA-41, Christy Holstege for AD-47, Lisa Middleton for SD-19, and Chris Shoults for AD-63**
---
|
---
| **Organizing for Derek Tran for CA-45**
---
|
---
| **Organizing for Dave Min for CA-47**
---
|
---
| **Cheryl S. Davis**
I was born in Philadelphia and moved to California in 1982 to attend graduate school at UC Davis, eventually settling in Folsom. While I now call California home, I remain a dedicated fan of Philadelphia sports teams. Growing up in a blue-collar, Democratic family, I began my social services career at 19 in a residential program for girls. I earned my Bachelor's degree in sociology from St. Joseph's College in Philadelphia.
After graduation, I cycled from Vancouver to San Diego, which deepened my love for Northern California. Following graduate school, I worked in youth residential programs and was among the first hires for Sacramento's Homeless Programs. Over 26 years, I held various roles in human services, including Human Assistance Director for Sacramento County and Human Services Director for Placer County, retiring as a liaison for the Affordable Care Act's implementation.
My passion for activism started early; I vividly remember being kissed by John F. Kennedy at three. I organized family boycotts for farmworkers, and my mother served as a poll worker until age 75. As a lifelong Democrat, my parents had me register to vote at 18.
As the Political Action Chair for the Folsom Area Democratic Club, I am committed to strengthening the Democratic presence in California. We are actively recruiting candidates for local offices and supporting Democratic candidates for assembly and Congress. With potential Democratic representation on our City Council in 2024, we engage in canvassing, phone banking, postcard parties, and voter registration events to elect Democrats across Folsom.
---

Peter,
I remember it like it was yesterday. The desert was freezing under the cover of night. I was briefing my team on the mission. I warned them that we may not all come out alive - but that we had to keep pushing on no matter what. We were going after one of the most wanted men in the Taliban, and if we could succeed in this mission, America - and the rest of the world - would be stronger and safer. My name is Col. Mike Waltz. For years I served as a Green Beret in some of the most dangerous war zones in the world. That night, we succeeded in our mission. But with terrorists growing stronger, we knew it was just the beginning of our work. Under Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, America’s enemies are gaining ground while we bend the knee to terrorists and dictators. It’s not right - and it’s not what I put my life on the line for. Now, I’m the first and only Green Beret to serve in Congress, and I’ve spent my time working hand-in-hand with President Trump to make America strong again. _But between my service to our country and my loyalty to President Trump and the MAGA movement, the radical Left has it out for me._ **[I’m on a mission to defeat them, but I need your help. clean_body: | | | Peter, I remember it like it was yesterday. The desert was freezing under the cover of night. I was briefing my team on the mission. I warned them that we may not all come out alive - but that we had to keep pushing on no matter what. We were going after one of the most wanted men in the Taliban, and if we could succeed in this mission, America - and the rest of the world - would be stronger and safer. My name is Col. Mike Waltz. For years I served as a Green Beret in some of the most dangerous war zones in the world. That night, we succeeded in our mission. But with terrorists growing stronger, we knew it was just the beginning of our work. Under Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, America’s enemies are gaining ground while we bend the knee to terrorists and dictators. It’s not right - and it’s not what I put my life on the line for. Now, I’m the first and only Green Beret to serve in Congress, and I’ve spent my time working hand-in-hand with President Trump to make America strong again. But between my service to our country and my loyalty to President Trump and the MAGA movement, the radical Left has it out for me. Right now, America needs strong leaders. We have President Trump. But he needs an A-Team in Congress he can count on to put in the work and put his plans to make America great into action. From day one in Congress, I’ve been his right-hand man. name: Dr. Ben Carson
subject: Join the fight to protect the unborn
body:
I feel like our culture has forgotten—or ignored—some very important... | _Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this[link](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/e/encryptedUnsubscribe?_r=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_s=099f88285ffc43d2bc1661dbd23a52db&_t=l3SV__DV7bsu284KZ-S_bBEtpNJpR5Vx2M9dcJIhF5-Ks8d_W1Civzb3_rb_NLKlJMFqd-viNk3CsK1CHV53UKkfaqBFfnr5TX4zs9kilLRg1hmBHexU7OUQWeQN3Oxk)_

---
| | | [](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=099f88285ffc43d2bc1661dbd23a52db&_e=24JDv2QKlKOYkkAfsRYLEgT9_L1sw2e4OUD1Hr0FRD2wVvA6BhMyw0M3QZLirGDpNtOsn8XEnBfF5y4uZfjCpOOQ7U4OiT1LcdAPHlpQkIjGFBLtyQQ0195VMp1q7WK3Olof_Ng3KAd6JRNNIG4TdDEmqMXm-56Zdn-IDbFx27KogwhxmPBEszyk_TUyZXbi1O-FD_730BYMbKu3BZLd5jvpbcRB4BsdIdqTJPodhhpBh6Zldojzsl7yjqMD6cAM6ExArwWN2LAPer1GJs9t3wL0NU6iMV4L_IuDD18Imn_bUnvcr52X_VCodhR7dslgDY2-QJYaED5__hNnNoCTNmvleIVW-nvhQirQFxJQ3YjbYaDWIIeFYmpUVqrDuwo2UCA7OnIgDOUVl3MMEC1_nAv1J_p-qjqNmkb6cldS-C4%3D)
---
| Fellow Patriot,

I feel like our culture has forgotten--or ignored--some very important and basic lessons when it comes to the development of human life.

Our society has been infected by an anti-life ideology, treating its most vulnerable members as disposable objects. Abortion that was once thought of as a last resort in a medical emergency has become the new normal.

Medicine tells us that life begins at the moment of conception. It also tells us when an unborn baby develops a heartbeat, brainwaves, and nervous system. Yet, despite all of this, the unborn are not treated as though they are alive or even human. [](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=099f88285ffc43d2bc1661dbd23a52db&_e=24JDv2QKlKOYkkAfsRYLEgT9_L1sw2e4OUD1Hr0FRD2wVvA6BhMyw0M3QZLirGDpNtOsn8XEnBfF5y4uZfjCpOOQ7U4OiT1LcdAPHlpQkIjGFBLtyQQ0195VMp1q7WK3Olof_Ng3KAd6JRNNIG4TdDEmqMXm-56Zdn-IDbFx27KogwhxmPBEszyk_TUyZXbi1O-FD_730BYMbKu3BZLd5jvpbcRB4BsdIdqTJPodhhpBh6Zldojzsl7yjqMD6cAM6ExArwWN2LAPer1GJs9t3_qtJHhu64G5fWaTVEgGLPvJ--_kBMttnw5I8_fhekHYtcGBKvLDffcZ4ApOv2m0nJk_q0BJD9nfquafNzb-1Ek2Yc8DHKPu9bzsTLE2sZDiIxSFrgwGEi0e9ZpxxoPOwHtiwmLPxDO3IHw7_UlNGjA%3D) **As a surgeon, I have operated on infants pre-birth. I can assure you that they are very much alive.**

Life is a precious gift that has been given to us from our creator. No person is disposable, and every life is precious according to Him.

I believe that everyone deserves life, even those who have been denied this right by our society. I believe that together we can make a difference and bring dignity and a voice to the unborn. I also believe that I'm not alone in this belief.

I believe that you believe that too.

I've started working with a group of like-minded individuals who are looking to change our culture. We want to build a society that values life but that takes people like you and I making a commitment.

The first step is clearly stating what we believe and what we are willing to do to protect the lives of the unborn. **[**Will you join me today and stand up for those who cannot do it for themselves?**](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=099f88285ffc43d2bc1661dbd23a52db&_e=24JDv2QKlKOYkkAfsRYLEgT9_L1sw2e4OUD1Hr0FRD2wVvA6BhMyw0M3QZLirGDpNtOsn8XEnBfF5y4uZfjCpOOQ7U4OiT1LcdAPHlpQkIjGFBLtyQQ0195VMp1q7WK3Olof_Ng3KAd6JRNNIG4TdDEmqMXm-56Zdn-IDbFx27KogwhxmPBEszyk_TUyZXbi1O-FD_730BYMbKu3BZLd5jvpbcRB4BsdIdqTJPodhhpBh6Zldojzsl7yjqMD6cAM6ExArwWN2LAPer1GJs9t3wjoDlAcYGGrDkYE5dt-ymq0tadKeodSDA-xMK8JyNefzYpHp70d5AmVYOqKXldul-BKV67CUkRYM7kpFnLBD6EwzjuDth2dKSvUwYyQp6skbRS4IUQhBpI0QPgwfCc0mz9qlhVwjyQ3fMg2pM3FR-w%3D)**

I've created a new pro-life pledge; I'd love your support. Would you read the pledge below to see if you align with our shared goals and are willing to commit to fighting for the lives of the unborn?

[https://offers.americancornerstone.org/pro-life-statement/](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=099f88285ffc43d2bc1661dbd23a52db&_e=24JDv2QKlKOYkkAfsRYLEgT9_L1sw2e4OUD1Hr0FRD2wVvA6BhMyw0M3QZLirGDpNtOsn8XEnBfF5y4uZfjCpOOQ7U4OiT1LcdAPHlpQkIjGFBLtyQQ0195VMp1q7WK3Olof_Ng3KAd6JRNNIG4TdDEmqMXm-56Zdn-IDbFx27KogwhxmPBEszyk_TUyZXbi1O-FD_730BYMbKu3BZLd5jvpbcRB4BsdIdqTJPodhhpBh6Zldojzsl7yjqMD6cAM6ExArwWN2LAPer1GJs9t322x6Rin74UCo3KK0eY8FGvQpwOfg5gNglmlZttK6IfHHdWqb6kuxBIx9BoQ58PSQDBDslxXprUwFVTFNlA-OJw6Hq-LMq3Y6T1q6iuINKktLq5WBvQl5y8Z-K8xUcJcGzHu2tx6fOKYP9HfQCoUJYk%3D)

Regards,

Dr. Ben Carson
Founder & Chairman
American Cornerstone Institute

Peter, I need to be
upfront about a risky decision our campaign made and why your support is
so urgent.

Republicans have ramped up vicious attack ads against me as they seek to
flip Wisconsin red and deliver the Senate majority for Republicans — and
Mitch McConnnell’s super PAC just launched an eight-figure ad blitz on top
of that. I hate to admit, but their strategy is gaining traction.

Too many recent polls to count show Eric Hovde and me locked in a
statistical tie. Multiple elections experts have shifted our race in
Republicans’ direction.

We can’t let this massive ad blitz go unanswered. We’re being outspent 2:1
and there’s no signs of that changing before Election Day. If we do
nothing, Hovde will continue his climb in the polls and could eventually
pull ahead in this toss-up Senate race.

That’s why we had to respond: We launched new campaign ads to set the
record straight and prevent Republicans from drowning us out.

The catch is, the money wasn’t in our original October budget. We’re now
facing a budget shortfall and we may not be able to keep our ads on the
air for long.

We made the risky decision to push forward anyway because staying silent
wasn’t an option — and I knew grassroots supporters like you have never
let us down when we’ve called on you to help us out.

**" Texas A&M International University president dies,"** Texas Tribune's**Kate McGee** -- "**Pablo Arenaz** , president of Texas A&M International University in Laredo, died unexpectedly Thursday night, the university said in a statement Friday.

Arenaz served as president of the 8,500 student university since 2016. He was 74-years-old.

No cause of death or additional information was immediately available, the university said in a press release.

"Texas A&M International University has thrived under Pablo," said **John Sharp** , Texas A&M University System chancellor, in a statement. "He was truly one of the best presidents in the country! He will be difficult to replace as a president and a friend!"

**Juan Castillo** , vice president of finance and administration, will handle day-to-day operations until an acting president is named. According to system rules, the chancellor can name an acting president until the Texas A&M System Board of Regents names an interim or new president.

Prior to becoming president, Arenaz served as university provost for eight years. He came to TAMIU from the University of Texas at El Paso, where he served in multiple administrative roles. He earned a bachelor's degree in education from the University of Nevada, Reno, as well as a masters degree. He earned a doctorate in genetics and cell biology from Washington State University.

**" What's new at UT's McCombs School of Business? Dean talks developments, entrepreneurship,"** Austin American-Statesman's**Lily Kepner** -- "By 9 a.m. on a Friday in September, 16 University of Texas students had gathered in the McCombs School of Business dean's conference room. They weren't in trouble, they weren't interviewing, and they weren't asking for extra credit. Instead, they had joined Dean **Lillian Mills** for breakfast tacos, orange juice and coffee to talk about their favorite nonbusiness class and ask her any questions they had brewing.

Mills became dean four years ago, and according to recently released U.S. News & World Report 2025 rankings, McCombs had the highest number of top-10 programs of all UT schools, with 12. The university's business programs tied for sixth place nationally and clinched first in Texas.

Over tinfoil-wrapped tacos, Mills, dressed in a burnt-orange suit, answered questions from the students about her daily routine (four shots of espresso after a 4:15 a.m. wake-up, a walk on the Forty Acres and a workout before work), her gratitude practice (texting five friends a day three things she's grateful for), how connected she is to the other deans (very) and what UT football games look like for her (15,000-step days gleefully greeting alumni and guests).

"Even deans have this 'Do I belong?' " fear, Mills confessed to the students gathered at the Sept. 27 Tacos with the Dean chat as she candidly and often vulnerably answered questions. It took her three years, she said, to realize she does belong.

Now, she wants the school she leads and the students within it to fasten and embrace relationships and resources across UT, leaning into collaboration and curiosity in business and beyond.

"Your job is to be the connector," she told them. "You need all of this richness to expand all the things you'll bring to your business you start one day."

In a sit-down interview with the American-Statesman three weeks into the start of the fall semester, Mills spoke about the new plans in the works at the ever-busy business school, updates to the planned new undergraduate business building, and the effect the top-ranked business programs have on students.

McCombs enrolled 948 new first-year students for the fall semester with an 11% acceptance rate. The current high-ranking programs put the school in a place to best help students, Mills said.

"What it signals is we're excellent at scale," Mills said. "Hardly any 18-year-old knows exactly what they want to do, particularly if you're like me and my parents weren't in business. ... What's great is you could come to Texas, not be 100% sure, but wherever you end up, you're at the top at that field."" **" Austin-based Tesla recalls more than 27,000 Cybertrucks for faulty rearview cameras,"** via Reuters**** -- "Tesla said Thursday that it would recall more than 27,000 Cybertrucks due to delayed rearview camera images that could impair driver visibility and increase crash risks, adding that a software update would resolve the issue.

The recall affects most Cybertrucks in the U.S. and is the biggest one for the electric truck. Tesla had issued a recall in [April](https://substack.com/redirect/a68bba16-3061-4867-83f4-b024f630bd45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to fix a loose accelerator pedal pad and another [in June](https://substack.com/redirect/29197bae-c3ac-46c0-b629-487cb696ab04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over issues with windshield wipers and exterior trim.

The electric vehicle maker started deliveries of the Cybertruck in November after a two-year delay due to production problems and battery supply constraints. Tesla has not disclosed Cybertruck production or delivery numbers.

Tesla CEO **Elon Musk** launched the "Blade Runner"-inspired truck to refresh the company's aging lineup amid slowing EV demand.

Issues with the model are closely watched by investors due to the resources Tesla has invested in its development.

The automaker said Thursday that the Cybertruck's system in the affected vehicles might not complete a shutdown process before it is commanded to boot up, resulting in a delay in displaying the rearview image.

The image might not appear within two seconds of placing the vehicle in reverse, and the display might appear blank for up to eight seconds when the vehicle is shifted into reverse, Tesla said in a report to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

The company said it identified the issue early last month, and all Cybertrucks currently in production have received the software fix." [Reuters](https://substack.com/redirect/765ab8da-4496-4e48-916d-1cf373dc68bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **LOCAL GOVERNMENT**

**" Houston council members pitch 5 percent property tax hike. Whitmire calls for no change,"** Houston Landing's **Hanna Holthaus** -- "Four city council members are proposing [a 5 percent increase](https://substack.com/redirect/23bb9030-c172-48fc-9652-765d4ec8128a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Houston's property tax rate they say would enable the city to avoid $86 million in spending cuts and bring in enough revenue to cover $40 million in cleanup costs left by the May derecho and Hurricane Beryl.

The increase, pitched by At-Large Councilmembers **Sally Alcorn** and **Leticia Plummer** , District H Councilmember **Mario Castillo** and District I Councilmember **Joaquin Martinez** , is one of two proposed rates on next week's council agenda.

Mayor **John Whitmire** is [proposing](https://substack.com/redirect/3e041594-f78e-4dfe-8b49-2ff0a94e9bd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to keep the tax rate at its current level of 51.9 cents per $100 of assessed value.

The rate being pushed by the four council members is 55.2 cents per $100 of assessed value.

The difference between the two proposals for the owner of a home valued at $300,000 with a standard 20 percent homestead exemption is about $78.

The proposals come less than a week after City Controller **Chris Hollins** warned officials to develop a plan to raise revenue or risk a downgrade in the city's overall credit rating.

Hollins said Friday he recommended the city publicize a plan to create a structurally balanced budget.

"This means cutting costs, bringing in more revenue, or some combination of both," Hollins said in a statement. "We also need to ensure that we are maintaining our reserves at levels comparable to those of other major cities. These reserves are critical when unexpected emergencies like Hurricane Beryl or the derecho storm impact Houston and the City has to quickly respond."

Following his remarks to council last week, members debated the merits of raising the tax rate, with Alcorn, Castillo and Martinez advocating for an increase.

The city's tax rate has decreased in nine of the past 10 years, but residents have not always felt that savings because of rising property values. Even with the same rate, some residents have paid more.

Council members have argued in previous meetings that the current tax rate is out of proportion for city needs and does not allow for the expansion or improvement of city services.

Under a 2004 voter-approved revenue cap, the city cannot increase its property tax collections more than 4.5 percent a year. A 2019 state law imposed a cap of 3.5 percent. The city would have to get voter approval to exceed that. The state cap, however, can be lifted to as high as 8 percent during periods of declared disasters." **" Will San Antonio allow VIA to add a tax to local cellphone bills?"** San Antonio Report's **Raquel Torres** -- "VIA Metropolitan Transit wants to add a tax to local phone bills to help it improve bus frequency and reduce wait times for riders.

The new line item on residents' and businesses' cellphone bills would run about 9 cents for every $100, VIA told City Council's Transportation and Infrastructure Committee last week, which agreed to send the request to the full council for approval.

The money VIA hopes to raise from the proposed tax, between $6 million and $8 million, would help fund its Better Bus Plan, which aims to shorten wait times for half of VIA's ridership from an hour to 30 minutes or less.

"We believe the impact to the cellphone user is minimal, but the impact to VIA and even the City of San Antonio can be significant," **Rod Sanchez** , VIA's senior vice president of planning and development, said at the Monday committee meeting.

But why is the local transit system asking the city to allow it to add this tax to local cellphone bills, given that it already receives a share of local sales tax from the city -- and is poised in January 2026 to get slightly more?

It's complicated, involving a tax on phone services that was taken away, then put back -- sort of. And it's also simple, said **Jon Gary Herrera** , VIA's senior vice president of public engagement.

VIA is "the most underfunded transit agency in Texas," he said, and is one of the last transit agencies to take advantage of the ability to add the cellphone bill tax to raise additional funds." * **2024**

**" Two of the hottest Texas House races this year are in San Antonio,"** San Antonio Express-News'**Leila Darwiche** -- "Texas doesn't have many competitive house districts, especially after the latest round of redistricting in 2021, when state lawmakers redrew the state's political maps. Under the new maps, only a handful of the 150 state house district races were competitive in the 2022 election and are thought to be in play again this November.

Two of those must-watch races are in San Antonio. They include District 118, which spans the city's south and west sides as well as much of Universal City and Live Oak, and District 121, which covers the north side, Alamo Heights and Olmos Park.

The Express-News analyzed historical election results, voter registration figures and data from the Census Bureau to see how these two districts have changed in the past decade and to explore why they've gotten more competitive.

**District 118**

For most of the 2010s, the district was held by Democrats, who consistently won by margins of over 10 points in general elections. However, the district was redrawn by the GOP-led Legislature in 2021 to include more of Live Oak and Universal City, and cut out areas surrounding Harlandale. As a result, in 2022, the district saw a much closer race.

Republican Rep. **John Lujan** defeated the Democratic candidate by a margin of 3.7 points, which amounted to just under 2,000 votes, to keep hold of the seat he won in a 2021 special election. It wasn't Rep. Lujan's first time holding the office: he represented the district for about a year [after narrowly winning another special election](https://substack.com/redirect/7f5b5aa5-9a86-4f91-9729-34da5dc79dfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - when turnout is usually depressed - in 2016 to replace**Joe Farias** , who vacated the seat early. In November, Lujan will face Democrat Kristian Carranza in what has [already been a contentious race](https://substack.com/redirect/3a402b31-fa68-4af7-8cc0-8d8a4f7cebdc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

**What 's changed?**

The data shows the new district map is more favorable to Republican candidates than it was before redistricting. For example, President **Joe Biden** won the district in 2020 by 13.7 points. If the new map had been in effect, Biden would have only won by 2.8 points.

The district has also seen demographic changes since 2014. Though the district still is made up mostly of Hispanic residents, they now comprise 66% of the district instead of the 74% before, while the district's share of white non-Hispanic residents increased by 5 percentage points. The district's share of residents over 65 and aged 25 to 34 have also grown.

The redistricting in 2021 played a large part in these changes. Under the old map, around 60% of registered voters had Spanish surnames but that share dropped to 48% under the new map, according to data from the Texas Legislative Council.

"The goal of Republicans in the Texas State legislature was to try to make [District] 118 more competitive for a Republican candidate," said Rice University Professor **Mark Jones**.

Republicans employed a strategy of including more white, non-Hispanic residents as well as Hispanic populations that might be more likely to vote Republican or not at all, said Jones.

Over the last decade, the number of registered voters in the district has grown faster than the state average and quicker than its population - following a trend for many urban districts [along the I-35 corridor](https://substack.com/redirect/7a4b3049-c6e3-4591-b7e9-daf12d59b723?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). From 2014 to 2022, the number of registered voters in the district increased by 45%, from around 86,400 to 125,000. The state only saw 26% growth in registered voters over the same period.

Looking forward to the upcoming election, District 118 will likely face another close race, and one with higher turnout because of the presidential election. The percentage of registered voters in the district who made it to the ballot box in 2022 was the lowest it had been since 2014, when incumbent Democrat Farias ran unopposed. In past elections in this very district, Democrat leaders [have pointed to low turnout](https://substack.com/redirect/ac762170-532a-403b-89a9-647808757e98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as the reason why Republicans managed to flip the district.

**District 121**

House District 121 was held for a decade by Republican **Joe Straus** , the former speaker of the Texas House. When the seat opened up in 2018, the district saw a Democrat on the ballot in a general election for the first time since 2000. Since then, the races' margins have been increasingly tighter. In 2020, District 121 had its first race that was decided within 7 points since at least 1992, the margin often used by political scientists [to determine the competitiveness](https://substack.com/redirect/c6105340-0f25-41c2-a399-8c5eea08740e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of an electoral district. In that election, Republican incumbent **Steve Allison** [defeated](https://substack.com/redirect/d0c3d70e-3c9a-44d1-9783-11eff0baf380?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Democrat **Celina Montoya **by just under 7 points.

After redistricting, the district now encompasses more area to San Antonio's north, including parts of Timberwood Park and other unincorporated areas in Bexar County. Under this new map in the 2022 election, Allison widened his margin to [10 points over](https://substack.com/redirect/376bf091-10c9-4eb5-85e9-fdb06a5daccf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Democratic challenger **Becca Defelice** , a margin that was greater than his wins in both 2018 and 2020. This larger margin speaks to a broader trend [where redistricting efforts made some races less competitive](https://substack.com/redirect/9c16b00a-6a82-4a90-aaa5-5031f101a425?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) statewide.

According to Jones, House Republicans' aim was to make District 121 a safe, red district. Under the old district map, Biden narrowly won in 2020, receiving 50.6% of the vote. If the new, redistricted map had been in effect, Trump would have actually won the district with 50.4% of the vote.

Though Jones said the 2021 redistricting "safeguarded" the district for Republicans, its voters' support for the party has wavered over time. If we take a long view of how the district voted in statewide races over the last decade, it has become less Republican-leaning, even with redistricting. Abbott carried the district in 2022 under the current map but received a much smaller percentage of the district's votes than he did under the old map in 2018 or 2014.

"It's unlike most Republican districts. It wouldn't be able to survive a Democratic wave election or a very unpopular Republican candidate," said Jones. "But all other things being equal, Republicans should be able to hold on to 121."" **" State Rep. John Lujan fought off home intruder, new ad says,"** San Antonio Express-News'**Edward McKinley** -- "In a campaign advertisement released this week, state Rep. **John Lujan** shared a gruesome story of fighting off a home invader who slit the throat of his newborn son years ago.

The 30-second video is his campaign's first ad of this cycle as [he faces one of the most competitive reelection bids](https://substack.com/redirect/62d704ed-a16e-47b6-a738-625a7d69b16f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of any member of the Texas Legislature.

In the ad, Lujan says the experience of protecting his own family makes him better equipped to fight for other people's families in the state Legislature. He cited examples, saying he increased healthcare for pregnant women, new mothers and babies and invested billions in border security.

Lujan was part of an overwhelming majority in the GOP-led House that voted last year to pass a Democrat-authored bill extending Medicaid to a full year postpartum. He also voted with most of the chamber for a [$321 billion state budget](https://substack.com/redirect/b7e1231a-c5dd-4b32-9339-b837032bf932?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that included $5 billion to support Gov. **Greg Abbott 's** border crackdown that has flooded South Texas with state troopers and soldiers who arrest migrants on criminal trespassing charges.

In a statement, Carranza said it's terrible to hear what Lujan's son went through. But she added that Lujan's stances, including on the state's abortion ban, don't reflect his promise to fight for families.

"If you say you support protecting families who rely on public schools, school lunch programs, or Medicaid then you can't vote against them in Austin," she said.

While Lujan, 62, has mentioned the home invasion before, he's never made it so central to his campaign.

In an interview with Hearst Newspapers, Lujan shared new details from that evening**,** as well as how he finally came to forgive the man who'd attacked his family, leaving his son badly injured and in need of surgery.

"The biggest impact that it had, I don't know why it sounds corny, but I wanted to share with everybody the power of forgiveness," Lujan said. "When people have true anger and hatefulness in their lives, it actually infects everything."" [SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/9eae1ca4-f9cf-486f-9456-295ade6e0407?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

**" Facing a tight race, Ted Cruz goes quiet on abortion,"** Texas Tribune's**Kayla Guo** -- "U.S. Sen. **Ted Cruz** has been a loud anti-abortion crusader throughout his political career.

But as reproductive rights loom over the election season as a key issue for voters, Cruz is uncharacteristically quiet.

The Texas Republican, running for a third term in the Senate, is locked in a tight race against U.S. Rep. **Colin Allred** , D-Dallas, who has made restoring access to abortion and blaming Cruz for the toppling of _Roe v. Wade_ central to his campaign.

This past week, Allred's campaign, boosted by an influx of cash from Senate Democrats, began airing an ad on TV and streaming platforms across the state that blasted Cruz for his anti-abortion record.

Texas has [banned almost all abortions](https://substack.com/redirect/3b2c850a-341b-4d41-bd62-c14a19503f70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- including in cases of rape and incest -- since Roe was overturned. Since then, Cruz has been more careful about how he engages on the topic. He has repeatedly called abortion a state issue, while offering more vocal support for in vitro fertilization.

Cruz, through a spokesperson, declined a request for an interview. The Texas Tribune reached out to his campaign eight times over six weeks to ask about his positions, posing nine initial questions via email and several follow ups on topics ranging from his past support for a national abortion ban to how he squares his belief in fetal personhood with his support for IVF -- a process which routinely involves the disposal of fertilized embryos.

Cruz's campaign did not respond directly to questions, instead providing links to previous statements he had made on the topic in other interviews. Those statements did not address several specific questions.

While Democrats have not won statewide in Texas in 30 years, the issue could pose a risk for Cruz, who squeaked to victory in 2018 against Beto O'Rourke by less than three percentage points. Though polling shows Texans [prioritizing issues](https://substack.com/redirect/e16e59fd-6a16-44df-b965-02ac39a87d85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) like border security and the economy over abortion, more Texans believe that the [state's abortion laws are too strict](https://substack.com/redirect/666d94c8-6496-4751-9f09-f3f34e9550a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and Democrats are banking on the issue boosting turnout nationwide in a presidential election year." ($5/mo or $50/yr or $199 lifetime) TOP NEWS " Texas A&M International University president dies," Texas Tribune'sKate McGee -- "Pablo Arenaz , president of Texas A&M International University in Laredo, died unexpectedly Thursday night, the university said in a statement Friday. Arenaz served as president of the 8,500 student university since 2016. He was 74-years-old. No cause of death or additional information was immediately available, the university said in a press release. "Texas A&M International University has thrived under Pablo," said John Sharp , Texas A&M University System chancellor, in a statement. "He was truly one of the best presidents in the country! He will be difficult to replace as a president and a friend!" Juan Castillo , vice president of finance and administration, will handle day-to-day operations until an acting president is named. According to system rules, the chancellor can name an acting president until the Texas A&M System Board of Regents names an interim or new president. Prior to becoming president, Arenaz served as university provost for eight years. He came to TAMIU from the University of Texas at El Paso, where he served in multiple administrative roles. He earned a bachelor's degree in education from the University of Nevada, Reno, as well as a masters degree. He earned a doctorate in genetics and cell biology from Washington State University. During his time as president, he spent his time increasing opportunities for the majority Hispanic student population, including curricular activity, internships and research opportunities, the university said. He also oversaw growth in science, technology, engineering and math fields, as well as health sciences. "On behalf of all TAMIU faculty, staff and students, we are all profoundly saddened by the passing of Dr. Arenaz," said Claudia San Miguel , provost at TAMIU, in a statement. "He was kind and generous and a leader we all admired. It is difficult to imagine this campus, this community, without his larger-than-life presence."" " What's new at UT's McCombs School of Business? Dean talks developments, entrepreneurship," Austin American-Statesman'sLily Kepner -- "By 9 a.m. on a Friday in September, 16 University of Texas students had gathered in the McCombs School of Business dean's conference room. They weren't in trouble, they weren't interviewing, and they weren't asking for extra credit. Instead, they had joined Dean Lillian Mills for breakfast tacos, orange juice and coffee to talk about their favorite nonbusiness class and ask her any questions they had brewing. Mills became dean four years ago, and according to recently released U.S. News & World Report 2025 rankings, McCombs had the highest number of top-10 programs of all UT schools, with 12. The university's business programs tied for sixth place nationally and clinched first in Texas. Over tinfoil-wrapped tacos, Mills, dressed in a burnt-orange suit, answered questions from the students about her daily routine (four shots of espresso after a 4:15 a.m. wake-up, a walk on the Forty Acres and a workout before work), her gratitude practice (texting five friends a day three things she's grateful for), how connected she is to the other deans (very) and what UT football games look like for her (15,000-step days gleefully greeting alumni and guests). "Even deans have this 'Do I belong?' " fear, Mills confessed to the students gathered at the Sept. 27 Tacos with the Dean chat as she candidly and often vulnerably answered questions. It took her three years, she said, to realize she does belong. Now, she wants the school she leads and the students within it to fasten and embrace relationships and resources across UT, leaning into collaboration and curiosity in business and beyond. "Your job is to be the connector," she told them. "You need all of this richness to expand all the things you'll bring to your business you start one day." In a sit-down interview with the American-Statesman three weeks into the start of the fall semester, Mills spoke about the new plans in the works at the ever-busy business school, updates to the planned new undergraduate business building, and the effect the top-ranked business programs have on students. McCombs enrolled 948 new first-year students for the fall semester with an 11% acceptance rate. The current high-ranking programs put the school in a place to best help students, Mills said. "What it signals is we're excellent at scale," Mills said. "Hardly any 18-year-old knows exactly what they want to do, particularly if you're like me and my parents weren't in business. ... What's great is you could come to Texas, not be 100% sure, but wherever you end up, you're at the top at that field."" ($) BUSINESS NEWS " Austin-based Tesla recalls more than 27,000 Cybertrucks for faulty rearview cameras," via Reuters** -- "Tesla said Thursday that it would recall more than 27,000 Cybertrucks due to delayed rearview camera images that could impair driver visibility and increase crash risks, adding that a software update would resolve the issue. The recall affects most Cybertrucks in the U.S. and is the biggest one for the electric truck. Tesla had issued a recall in to fix a loose accelerator pedal pad and another over issues with windshield wipers and exterior trim. The electric vehicle maker started deliveries of the Cybertruck in November after a two-year delay due to production problems and battery supply constraints. Tesla has not disclosed Cybertruck production or delivery numbers. Tesla CEO Elon Musk launched the "Blade Runner"-inspired truck to refresh the company's aging lineup amid slowing EV demand. Issues with the model are closely watched by investors due to the resources Tesla has invested in its development. The automaker said Thursday that the Cybertruck's system in the affected vehicles might not complete a shutdown process before it is commanded to boot up, resulting in a delay in displaying the rearview image. The image might not appear within two seconds of placing the vehicle in reverse, and the display might appear blank for up to eight seconds when the vehicle is shifted into reverse, Tesla said in a report to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The company said it identified the issue early last month, and all Cybertrucks currently in production have received the software fix." LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Houston council members pitch 5 percent property tax hike. Whitmire calls for no change," Houston Landing's Hanna Holthaus -- "Four city council members are proposing in Houston's property tax rate they say would enable the city to avoid $86 million in spending cuts and bring in enough revenue to cover $40 million in cleanup costs left by the May derecho and Hurricane Beryl. The increase, pitched by At-Large Councilmembers Sally Alcorn and Leticia Plummer , District H Councilmember Mario Castillo and District I Councilmember Joaquin Martinez , is one of two proposed rates on next week's council agenda. Mayor John Whitmire is to keep the tax rate at its current level of 51.9 cents per $100 of assessed value. The rate being pushed by the four council members is 55.2 cents per $100 of assessed value. The difference between the two proposals for the owner of a home valued at $300,000 with a standard 20 percent homestead exemption is about $78. The proposals come less than a week after City Controller Chris Hollins warned officials to develop a plan to raise revenue or risk a downgrade in the city's overall credit rating. Hollins said Friday he recommended the city publicize a plan to create a structurally balanced budget. "This means cutting costs, bringing in more revenue, or some combination of both," Hollins said in a statement. "We also need to ensure that we are maintaining our reserves at levels comparable to those of other major cities. These reserves are critical when unexpected emergencies like Hurricane Beryl or the derecho storm impact Houston and the City has to quickly respond." Following his remarks to council last week, members debated the merits of raising the tax rate, with Alcorn, Castillo and Martinez advocating for an increase. The city's tax rate has decreased in nine of the past 10 years, but residents have not always felt that savings because of rising property values. Even with the same rate, some residents have paid more. Council members have argued in previous meetings that the current tax rate is out of proportion for city needs and does not allow for the expansion or improvement of city services. Under a 2004 voter-approved revenue cap, the city cannot increase its property tax collections more than 4.5 percent a year. A 2019 state law imposed a cap of 3.5 percent. The city would have to get voter approval to exceed that. The state cap, however, can be lifted to as high as 8 percent during periods of declared disasters." " Will San Antonio allow VIA to add a tax to local cellphone bills?" San Antonio Report's Raquel Torres -- "VIA Metropolitan Transit wants to add a tax to local phone bills to help it improve bus frequency and reduce wait times for riders. The new line item on residents' and businesses' cellphone bills would run about 9 cents for every $100, VIA told City Council's Transportation and Infrastructure Committee last week, which agreed to send the request to the full council for approval. The money VIA hopes to raise from the proposed tax, between $6 million and $8 million, would help fund its Better Bus Plan, which aims to shorten wait times for half of VIA's ridership from an hour to 30 minutes or less. "We believe the impact to the cellphone user is minimal, but the impact to VIA and even the City of San Antonio can be significant," Rod Sanchez , VIA's senior vice president of planning and development, said at the Monday committee meeting. But why is the local transit system asking the city to allow it to add this tax to local cellphone bills, given that it already receives a share of local sales tax from the city -- and is poised in January 2026 to get slightly more? It's complicated, involving a tax on phone services that was taken away, then put back -- sort of. And it's also simple, said Jon Gary Herrera , VIA's senior vice president of public engagement. VIA is "the most underfunded transit agency in Texas," he said, and is one of the last transit agencies to take advantage of the ability to add the cellphone bill tax to raise additional funds." 2024 " Two of the hottest Texas House races this year are in San Antonio," San Antonio Express-News'Leila Darwiche -- "Texas doesn't have many competitive house districts, especially after the latest round of redistricting in 2021, when state lawmakers redrew the state's political maps. Under the new maps, only a handful of the 150 state house district races were competitive in the 2022 election and are thought to be in play again this November. Two of those must-watch races are in San Antonio. They include District 118, which spans the city's south and west sides as well as much of Universal City and Live Oak, and District 121, which covers the north side, Alamo Heights and Olmos Park. The Express-News analyzed historical election results, voter registration figures and data from the Census Bureau to see how these two districts have changed in the past decade and to explore why they've gotten more competitive. District 118 For most of the 2010s, the district was held by Democrats, who consistently won by margins of over 10 points in general elections. However, the district was redrawn by the GOP-led Legislature in 2021 to include more of Live Oak and Universal City, and cut out areas surrounding Harlandale. As a result, in 2022, the district saw a much closer race. Republican Rep. John Lujan defeated the Democratic candidate by a margin of 3.7 points, which amounted to just under 2,000 votes, to keep hold of the seat he won in a 2021 special election. It wasn't Rep. Lujan's first time holding the office: he represented the district for about a year - when turnout is usually depressed - in 2016 to replaceJoe Farias , who vacated the seat early. In November, Lujan will face Democrat Kristian Carranza in what has . What 's changed? The data shows the new district map is more favorable to Republican candidates than it was before redistricting. For example, President Joe Biden won the district in 2020 by 13.7 points. If the new map had been in effect, Biden would have only won by 2.8 points. The district has also seen demographic changes since 2014. Though the district still is made up mostly of Hispanic residents, they now comprise 66% of the district instead of the 74% before, while the district's share of white non-Hispanic residents increased by 5 percentage points. The district's share of residents over 65 and aged 25 to 34 have also grown. The redistricting in 2021 played a large part in these changes. Under the old map, around 60% of registered voters had Spanish surnames but that share dropped to 48% under the new map, according to data from the Texas Legislative Council. "The goal of Republicans in the Texas State legislature was to try to make [District] 118 more competitive for a Republican candidate," said Rice University Professor Mark Jones. Republicans employed a strategy of including more white, non-Hispanic residents as well as Hispanic populations that might be more likely to vote Republican or not at all, said Jones. Over the last decade, the number of registered voters in the district has grown faster than the state average and quicker than its population - following a trend for many urban districts . From 2014 to 2022, the number of registered voters in the district increased by 45%, from around 86,400 to 125,000. The state only saw 26% growth in registered voters over the same period. Looking forward to the upcoming election, District 118 will likely face another close race, and one with higher turnout because of the presidential election. The percentage of registered voters in the district who made it to the ballot box in 2022 was the lowest it had been since 2014, when incumbent Democrat Farias ran unopposed. In past elections in this very district, Democrat leaders as the reason why Republicans managed to flip the district. District 121 House District 121 was held for a decade by Republican Joe Straus , the former speaker of the Texas House. When the seat opened up in 2018, the district saw a Democrat on the ballot in a general election for the first time since 2000. Since then, the races' margins have been increasingly tighter. In 2020, District 121 had its first race that was decided within 7 points since at least 1992, the margin often used by political scientists of an electoral district. In that election, Republican incumbent Steve Allison Democrat Celina Montoya by just under 7 points. After redistricting, the district now encompasses more area to San Antonio's north, including parts of Timberwood Park and other unincorporated areas in Bexar County. Under this new map in the 2022 election, Allison widened his margin to Democratic challenger Becca Defelice , a margin that was greater than his wins in both 2018 and 2020. This larger margin speaks to a broader trend statewide. According to Jones, House Republicans' aim was to make District 121 a safe, red district. Under the old district map, Biden narrowly won in 2020, receiving 50.6% of the vote. If the new, redistricted map had been in effect, Trump would have actually won the district with 50.4% of the vote. Though Jones said the 2021 redistricting "safeguarded" the district for Republicans, its voters' support for the party has wavered over time. If we take a long view of how the district voted in statewide races over the last decade, it has become less Republican-leaning, even with redistricting. Abbott carried the district in 2022 under the current map but received a much smaller percentage of the district's votes than he did under the old map in 2018 or 2014. "It's unlike most Republican districts. It wouldn't be able to survive a Democratic wave election or a very unpopular Republican candidate," said Jones. "But all other things being equal, Republicans should be able to hold on to 121."" ($) " State Rep. John Lujan fought off home intruder, new ad says," San Antonio Express-News'Edward McKinley -- "In a campaign advertisement released this week, state Rep. John Lujan shared a gruesome story of fighting off a home invader who slit the throat of his newborn son years ago. The 30-second video is his campaign's first ad of this cycle as of any member of the Texas Legislature. In the ad, Lujan says the experience of protecting his own family makes him better equipped to fight for other people's families in the state Legislature. He cited examples, saying he increased healthcare for pregnant women, new mothers and babies and invested billions in border security. Lujan was part of an overwhelming majority in the GOP-led House that voted last year to pass a Democrat-authored bill extending Medicaid to a full year postpartum. He also voted with most of the chamber for a that included $5 billion to support Gov. Greg Abbott 's border crackdown that has flooded South Texas with state troopers and soldiers who arrest migrants on criminal trespassing charges. In a statement, Carranza said it's terrible to hear what Lujan's son went through. But she added that Lujan's stances, including on the state's abortion ban, don't reflect his promise to fight for families. "If you say you support protecting families who rely on public schools, school lunch programs, or Medicaid then you can't vote against them in Austin," she said. While Lujan, 62, has mentioned the home invasion before, he's never made it so central to his campaign. In an interview with Hearst Newspapers, Lujan shared new details from that evening, as well as how he finally came to forgive the man who'd attacked his family, leaving his son badly injured and in need of surgery. "The biggest impact that it had, I don't know why it sounds corny, but I wanted to share with everybody the power of forgiveness," Lujan said. "When people have true anger and hatefulness in their lives, it actually infects everything."" ($) " Facing a tight race, Ted Cruz goes quiet on abortion," Texas Tribune'sKayla Guo -- "U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz has been a loud anti-abortion crusader throughout his political career. But as reproductive rights loom over the election season as a key issue for voters, Cruz is uncharacteristically quiet. The Texas Republican, running for a third term in the Senate, is locked in a tight race against U.S. Rep. Colin Allred , D-Dallas, who has made restoring access to abortion and blaming Cruz for the toppling of Roe v. Wade central to his campaign. This past week, Allred's campaign, boosted by an influx of cash from Senate Democrats, began airing an ad on TV and streaming platforms across the state that blasted Cruz for his anti-abortion record. Texas has -- including in cases of rape and incest -- since Roe was overturned. Since then, Cruz has been more careful about how he engages on the topic. He has repeatedly called abortion a state issue, while offering more vocal support for in vitro fertilization. Cruz, through a spokesperson, declined a request for an interview. The Texas Tribune reached out to his campaign eight times over six weeks to ask about his positions, posing nine initial questions via email and several follow ups on topics ranging from his past support for a national abortion ban to how he squares his belief in fetal personhood with his support for IVF -- a process which routinely involves the disposal of fertilized embryos. Cruz's campaign did not respond directly to questions, instead providing links to previous statements he had made on the topic in other interviews. Those statements did not address several specific questions. While Democrats have not won statewide in Texas in 30 years, the issue could pose a risk for Cruz, who squeaked to victory in 2018 against Beto O'Rourke by less than three percentage points. Though polling shows Texans like border security and the economy over abortion, more Texans believe that the , and Democrats are banking on the issue boosting turnout nationwide in a presidential election year." Hi there - It’s Eric.
**I’m going to be blunt: My opponent, Lisa Blunt Rochester, is jeopardizing the safety of all Delawareans. Why do I say that? Just a couple weeks ago, she voted against a bill that would have protected women against crimes committed by illegal immigrants.**
On September 19, Rochester [voted against](https://voteerichansen.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=507adf5d727e502cde205c852&id=86540f868d&e=dbd1068b05) the Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act, a bill that would require the deportation of illegal immigrants convicted of sex offenses, domestic violence, stalking child abuse, or violating a protection order.
Rochester joined other far-left progressive Democrats in voting against the bill. Unfortunately, it’s nothing new for her.
In 2017, she also voted against Kate’s Law, which would have imposed mandatory minimums for illegal immigrants who commit crimes after being deported and who re-enter the country illegally.
**> >> Time after time, Lisa Blunt Rochester votes in ways that put her constituents at risk. Her dangerous, soft-on-crime policies make everyone less safe. <<<**
Delaware deserves better, and as your next United States senator, you can bet I will vote differently.
[But I need your help. I need you to donate to my campaign today. Rochester’s soft-on-crime votes are outrageous and the only way they’re going to end is if we defeat her at the ballot box this November. ](https://voteerichansen.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=507adf5d727e502cde205c852&id=3d0822bdb1&e=dbd1068b05)
Every Delawarean deserves to be safe.[ **Can I count on you to step up today?**](https://voteerichansen.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=507adf5d727e502cde205c852&id=26de4b8cd5&e=dbd1068b05)

Arenaz served as president of the 8,500 student university since 2016. He was 74-years-old.

No cause of death or additional information was immediately available, the university said in a press release.

Peter, The Republicans are desperate. The old-fashioned and dark strategies they are employing are simply not working. Replacing well-thought out policy plans with waving swastika flags on the I-40/64 highway overpass isn’t too bright of an idea either. The crazy distractions are not only offensive, they are misleading, and can possibly negatively impact voter turnout on Tuesday, November 5th. Voter intimidation is at an all time high, too. Some conservative operatives are intentionally confusing college students about where they can vote without giving them the proper guidelines. Some college students, who are registered in other states, are being told there’s no need to update their voter status at school. For other students, they are not being told to request absentee ballots from their home states. Because I live right next to Washington University, this is what I am hearing every day. These impressionable students are trying to wade these treacherous political waters the best way they can. As they do so, they are still trying to make the best decisions for themselves and their futures. So basic and accurate information needs to get out to them and fast. That’s why I’ve been spending my extra time speaking with college students in my area to let them know what they need to do to vote and where to go. The exciting news is that students from must-win states like Michigan, Pennsylvania and Georgia are encouraged to request their home state absentee ballots. They know their vote matters. Conservative operatives are also attacking immigrant communities. Have you seen the dog and cat memes lately? Ohio has had to take lengthy measures to keep immigrant communities safe with the lies that are being spread about the culture and lifestyle of Haitian Americans who are legally in America. Conservatives are pushing other nonsensical distractions that may influence independents leaning towards voting for Democrats. Here’s the worst. Most of us have heard about the Sean “Diddy” Combs multi-tiered indictment in New York. Now conservative operatives are using social media platforms, including YouTube, TikTok, X and Facebook to try to tie prominent supporters of Kamala Harris and Tim Walz to Sean Combs. While the Combs’ situation carries an unsavory stench, conservative messaging is basically there’s a connection to the alleged horrific deeds of Sean Combs and our Democratic candidate. They've gone so far as to superimpose photos in an effort to tie Kamala Harris to this mess. Again, in my spare time, I’ve been trolling these conservative distractors to make sure it is clear our candidate has a vision for the future, tested policy plans and superior skill sets to move every American family forward. As I do my part to ensure Democrats win up-and-down the ballot in November, [**I am asking for your support TODAY to help recapture the losses from our unsuccessful primary campaign.**](http://clicksp.mariaformissouri.com/f/a/QWb5XFYpx-DJ8Auv62rh0Q~~/AAPPAAA~/RgRo5pFpP0SvaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL21hcmlhZm9ybWlzc291cmk_cmVmY29kZT13ZWJidG4mY2RtYz0ybW5IckZSR2pOcmRYTkVhMnZoeVhRZzVDYWMmcmVmY29kZTI9Mm1uSHJGUkdqTnJkWE5FYTJ2aHlYUWc1Q2FjJnJlZmNvZGVjZG1jPTJtbkhyRlJHak5yZFhORWEydmh5WFFnNUNhY1cDc3BjQgpm92kMBGc3XRSCUhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAAABtQ~~) Look, the November election is right around the corner. I am dedicated to fighting for Democracy and global sustainability. We can’t waste one moment. And we certainly will not go back!!! Thank you. See you at the polls! —Maria

subject: It’s the Senate, Stupid
disclaimer_text:

body:
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/p/vsbg6CJWNx
You've probably heard Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential campaign
slogan...
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/p/osbg6CJWNx

You've
probably heard Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential campaign slogan,
"It's the Economy, Stupid." Clinton's political strategist, James
Carville, posted it inside campaign headquarters to keep the team
focused and on the message.

The
slogan is making a comeback in 2024 as Republicans highlight
Kamala Harris's dismal economic record. But if you're a
freedom-loving American, we have a different slogan for you.

"It's the
Senate, Stupid."

Conservatives are rightly focused on the presidential race this
year, but winning the White House - as critical as it is - won't
be enough to save the country without a conservative Senate.
Without the Senate, President Trump won't be able to confirm his
appointees or enact his second-term agenda.

A
Republican president without a conservative Senate is simply a
waste of a Republican president.

That's
why we must take action right now to help elect the best Senate
candidates across the nation.

A
president can campaign on good policies, but he doesn't write the
bills. As long as liberals control the Senate, good legislation
will never be signed into law.

Does
anyone think Chuck Schumer will ever send bills to President
Trump's desk to secure our borders, grow our economy, expand
American energy, and restore election integrity?

Of course
not. If we fail to win the Senate, none of these common-sense
policies will be passed.

And if
Kamala Harris wins, we won't be able to stop Senate Democrats
from nuking the filibuster, passing their extreme agenda without
debate, and creating a permanent Democrat majority.

As we
head into the final days of this election, we must support the
conservatives running for U.S. Senate.

These
eight candidates believe in the principles of freedom that make
America great and are willing to fight for them. They aren't
liberal RINOs who will sell us out as soon as they're elected.

WIN THE
SENATE

Contribute to these Senate candidates and help push them on to
victory.

DONATE
NOW

These
Senate races will not receive the same media attention as the
presidential race, but they are no less important.

If you
agree that winning a conservative majority in the U.S. Senate is
vital to our nation's future, and if you're willing to engage in
these races even when the media ignores them, then please do two
things today.

(1)
Forward this email and encourage other conservatives to join our
grassroots effort to build a conservative Senate.

(2) Make
a split contribution to these candidates today. Without financial
support, they simply won't win.

Thank you
for considering this urgent request and for doing so much to help
fight for America's future.

We live
in the greatest country in the world, and if we work together, we
can preserve it for generations to come.

ELECTION
COUNTDOWN

SUPPORT
SENATE CONSERVATIVES

DONATE
NOW

name: Charlie Kirk, TPUSA
subject: The biggest and boldest Turning Point USA plan ever…
body:
TheFederalistWire.com

Please read the following message
from our sponsor.

Fellow American,

I've never seen anything like this.

Even at the start of the school year, Turning Point USA's
MISSION 2024 - our BIGGEST and BOLDEST youth effort EVER - is
already a MASSIVE SUCCESS.

We have already reached MILLIONS of young people with a
powerful, pro-America message ... and THOUSANDS of students are
turning out for Turning Point USA's most ambitious campus tour.

Fellow American, will you help Turning Point USA's MISSION 2024 keep
up our MASSIVE GROWTH and WINNING MOMENTUM? Your generous gift of
$20.24, $50, $100, or even $250 will have an IMMEDIATE impact on
our work!

Stand with Charlie & Turning Point USA

Above: More than 1,200 STUDENTS joined me at the University of
North Texas. You can see just some of the crowd in these video
screenshots!

Fellow American, in this all-important year for America's future,
Turning Point USA is launching a MASSIVE, ALL-HANDS-ON-DECK
effort to save our country: MISSION 2024.

Turning Point USA has already signed up THOUSANDS of new
student activists at high schools and colleges - and our
hard-working field representatives are recruiting EVEN MORE
America-loving young people in ALL 50 states.

And I am PERSONALLY visiting 21 schools across America from
now until November … and HUNDREDS and HUNDREDS of
patriotic kids are showing up for EVERY event!

To stand with me and Turning Point USA in this CRITICAL moment
for our country, please make your most generous gift of $20.24,
$50, or even $100 right now.

Stand with Charlie & Turning Point USA

Above: A Turning Point USA high school club had 95 STUDENTS
join their meeting - during which they started studying the
CONSTITUTION.

Fellow American, Turning Point USA's MISSION 2024 is sparking
GENERATIONAL CHANGE in favor of PATRIOTISM and AMERICAN
GREATNESS…

…and I don't want to let up on this MASSIVE GROWTH and
WINNING MOMENTUM for a moment!

Please make a generous gift to help Turning Point USA KEEP
WINNING with our MISSION 2024 initiative.

Fellow American, thank you for your patriotism, moral courage, and
support of Turning Point USA.

I can't wait to see how much more we will achieve together
through Turning Point USA as we do more than EVER BEFORE to
inspire the next generation to reject the toxic lies of the Left
and LOVE AMERICA again!

For America,

Charlie Kirk

Founder & CEO

Turning Point USA

Support Turning Point USA

4940 East Beverly Road

Phoenix, Arizona 85044
